entries.what_happened: Two OpenAI manuscripts in the family. (a) 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves' (Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026) claims three things. First, the 2-converse: for every E/Q whose full 2^∞-Selmer corank c₂(E) (local Kummer conditions at every place) is 0 or 1, ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = rank E(Q) = c₂(E), and Sha(E/Q) is finite. The proof splits into the case E(Q)[2] ≠ 0 and the case E[2] irreducible. Second, a finite-descent corollary: if d₂(E) = dim Sel₂(E/Q) − dim E(Q)[2] is 0 or 1, the same equalities hold and Sha(E/Q)[2^∞] = 0. Third, a density theorem: for every E/Q, the signed squarefree twist parameters d with analytic rank 0 and with analytic rank 1 each have density 1/2 among signed squarefree d ordered by |d|; for a density-one set of such d, analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks of E^(d) agree and Sha(E^(d)/Q) is finite. (b) 'The mean analytic rank of quadratic twists of elliptic curves' (The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-October-6-2026) proves that the mean analytic rank of the twists E^(d) tends to 1/2 in the same ordering. It takes the density theorem of (a) as its only input from (a) and adds its own tail estimate. It is about twists, not E itself, and says nothing about the leading coefficient.
entries.delivers: For every E/Q with c₂(E) ∈ {0,1}, with no restriction on reduction type, complex multiplication, rational torsion or rational isogeny, the manuscript establishes part (1), that algebraic rank equals the analytic order of vanishing, and part (3), finiteness of Sha(E/Q). The restriction that matters is c₂(E) ≤ 1, a bound on the full 2-power Selmer corank, not on the rank alone. For a general E, the density theorem gives rank equality and finiteness only for a density-one set of quadratic twists E^(d), not for E itself. The manuscript says its rank and finiteness assertions 'are distinct from the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula', so part (2), the leading-coefficient formula, is not established here. The introduction also cites a separate preprint, OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026 (Corollary 16.1), which with the density theorem gives the two-primary leading-coefficient formula on a density-one set of signed squarefree twists; the manuscript says this leading-coefficient assertion concerns the valuation at 2 only. That preprint is not in this family and is not read here. Neither manuscript says it settles Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct: (a) for every E/Q with c₂(E) ≥ 2, including every E whose 2-Selmer corank is at least two, equality of ord_{s=1}L(E,s) and rank E(Q) and finiteness of Sha(E/Q) are not addressed; (b) the leading-coefficient formula L^(r)(E,1)/r! = Ω_E · Reg_E · #Sha(E/Q) · ∏c_p / #E(Q)_tors² is not addressed for any E, beyond the 2-adic-valuation consequence on a density-one set of twists attributed to the other preprint; (c) in the list's own words, for E itself the statement is open whenever c₂(E) ≥ 2.
entries.direction: proves the rank and Sha-finiteness parts when the 2-Selmer corank is 0 or 1, and density statements for twists; leading-term formula not addressed
entries.conditional_on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in the 2-converse or in the density theorem as stated, and BSD is not assumed; the Heegner-section proof says 'no BSD equality is assumed'. Other sources the argument relies on: (i) the density theorem uses Smith's Theorem 1.1 on full 2^∞-Selmer coranks (Smith2025, a published result not in this family and not reproved here); the manuscript notes that Smith's analytic corollary assumes BSD, and says it does not use that corollary. (ii) The corank-zero case uses Kato's Beilinson–Kato class (Kato 2004). The corank-one case uses Heegner points with Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin, Waldspurger's formula, and Howard's Kolyvagin-system framework. Monsky, Cassels and Tate are cited for 2-descent parity and isogeny invariance. (iii) The two-primary leading-coefficient consequence in the introduction depends on OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026 (Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 16.1), a different manuscript that is not read here. The proof sections of this manuscript cite no other OpenAI manuscript. The mean-rank manuscript uses the density theorem only for its mean result.
entries.doubts: (1) The rank statement is restricted to c₂(E) ≤ 1 and says nothing for E with c₂(E) ≥ 2; the manuscripts do not present themselves as settling Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer. (2) The leading-coefficient consequence is attributed to another preprint and, in this text, is only a 2-adic valuation statement about twists. (3) Without marking any step as sketched, the text flags its delicate points. In the irreducible-E[2] construction the coefficient test 'does not identify the coefficient test with the determinant' and is linked to it only by a sum-zero relation. The odd-sign coefficient selection is described as a minimum over bounded-weight sequences as precision grows, with each finite collection of tests 'realized at a sufficiently high actual precision'. (4) The proof runs to about 9,300 lines of TeX across the section files. Reader's note, not a claim of the text: I read the statements, the reduction steps and some of the constructions, not all of them, so I have not checked the middle sections.

entries.what_happened: Neither manuscript mentions congruent numbers or Tunnell's theorem. The link runs through E₀: y² = x³ − x. Its twist by a squarefree d is E₀^(d): d·y² = x³ − x, which over Q is y² = x³ − d²x (substitute X = dx, Y = d²y). For n > 0 squarefree this is the congruent-number curve E_n: y² = x³ − n²x. Both manuscripts apply to E₀ as they apply to any E/Q. The Goldfeld-density manuscript (Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026) gives the 2-converse and the density theorem described under the BSD entry. The mean-rank manuscript (The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-October-6-2026) gives mean analytic rank 1/2 over signed squarefree twists of E₀. The following is my derivation from those theorems. It is not stated in either manuscript. (i) Because E₀^(n) and E₀^(−n) are the same curve, the signed counts split evenly between positive and negative n, so the density statements hold over positive squarefree n with the same values: analytic rank 0 and analytic rank 1 each have density 1/2, and c₂ ∈ {0,1} has density one. (ii) For positive squarefree n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}, the 2-converse gives ord_{s=1}L(E_n,s) = rank E_n(Q) = c₂(E_n). Since n is congruent exactly when E_n(Q) has positive rank (the standard equivalence for squarefree n, where E_n(Q) has torsion (Z/2)²), we get: n is congruent ⇔ c₂(E_n) = 1 ⇔ L(E_n,1) = 0. No BSD assumption is used. The classical Tunnell route needs BSD for the step 'L(E_n,1) = 0 implies n congruent'; for n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1} this manuscript supplies that step unconditionally. (iii) The set of n with c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 has density zero, since Smith's count, which the Goldfeld manuscript uses, makes c₂ ∈ {0,1} density one. Together with (i) and (ii), this gives that congruent numbers have asymptotic density 1/2 among positive squarefree integers.
entries.delivers: Restricted to positive squarefree n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}, the family decides congruence unconditionally, with 'congruent' equal to 'L(E_n,1) = 0' and to '2-Selmer corank 1' (step ii above). The family's own statements give density 1/2 for analytic rank 0 and for analytic rank 1 among the twists of E₀, and by (i) and (iii), density 1/2 for congruent numbers among positive squarefree integers. These are asymptotic statements. They do not say whether any particular n is congruent, and they do not give a procedure that decides every n. The problem asks to 'determine precisely what rational numbers are congruent numbers'. This family does not meet that demand, which needs a criterion for every n.
entries.remains: (a) A criterion that decides every n. For n with c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 nothing is said, and the family gives no computation of c₂(E_n) for any particular n. (b) The density-zero exceptional set where c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 is not resolved. (c) Tunnell's L-value criterion is neither stated nor proved in these manuscripts, so the problem's named route is not reproduced here. (d) Non-integral rationals: the manuscripts say nothing about them. The reduction to positive squarefree integers is the literature's convention, and the problem's literal 'rational numbers' wording is not addressed.
entries.direction: proves a density statement for the congruent-number twist family and, for c₂ ∈ {0,1}, unconditional identification of congruence with rank one (derived here); decides no individual n
entries.conditional_on: Step (ii) uses the 2-converse for E_n, which applies only where c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}; the manuscripts give no way to check that for a given n. The density statements use Smith2025 Theorem 1.1 (external, not reproved here). The facts 'congruent ⇔ positive rank for squarefree n' and 'E_n(Q) has torsion (Z/2)²' are standard results used from outside the family. The rest of the dependencies are as in the BSD entry: Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin, Kato, Waldspurger, Howard, Monsky and Cassels.
entries.doubts: (1) No manuscript mentions congruent numbers, Tunnell's theorem, or the density of congruent numbers. Steps (i) to (iii) are my derivation from the stated theorems and should be weighed as such. (2) The density theorems are stated for the signed count. The reduction to positive n uses E₀^(n) = E₀^(−n), which I checked from the twist formula; the manuscripts do not state it. (3) The Goldfeld manuscript's introduction cites congruent-number literature (Tian; Smith; Kriz; and BurungaleTian2026, Theorem 1.2, which gives rank zero for almost all positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8 in the family n·y² = x³ − x). These are cited as background, and the family does not rely on them. (4) The density statements are asymptotic, and nothing in the text says which n are congruent.
